binders: c : ℝ is the existentially chosen universal constant.
ι is an arbitrary finite type indexing the family.
Ω is an arbitrary measurable sample space.
μ is a probability measure on Ω.
X : ι → Ω → ℝ assigns to every i a real-valued function X_i on Ω.
m M : ι → ℝ assign lower and upper endpoints m_i and M_i.
t : ℝ is the upper-tail threshold.
hypotheses: For every i ∈ ι, X_i is measurable from Ω to the Borel measurable real line.
The indexed family of functions X is mutually independent under μ.
For every i ∈ ι, X_i(ω) ∈ [m_i,M_i] for μ-almost every ω; the exceptional null set may depend on i, although finiteness permits simultaneous almost-everywhere bounds.
S = ∑_{i∈ι} ‖M_i-m_i‖² > 0; because the real norm is absolute value, S = ∑_{i∈ι}|M_i-m_i|².
conclusions: Let E = {ω ∈ Ω | ∑_{i∈ι}(X_i(ω) - ∫_Ω X_i(y) dμ(y)) ≥ t}. Then μ.real(E) ≤ 2 · exp(-(c · t²)/S), where μ.real(E) is the real conversion of the extended-nonnegative-real measure μ(E). Since μ is a probability measure, this is the ordinary real-valued probability of E.
mathematical_definitions: ∃ c : ℝ, c > 0 ∧ ∀ finite ι, measurable Ω, probability measures μ, families X : ι → Ω → ℝ, bounds m M : ι → ℝ, and t : ℝ, measurability of every X_i → mutual independence of X under μ → almost-everywhere interval bounds for every X_i → t > 0 → ∑_i |M_i-M_i+(M_i-m_i)|² > 0 as actually written equivalently ∑_i |M_i-m_i|² > 0 → the displayed upper-tail bound.
The existential quantifier for c is outermost, so one and the same positive c must work uniformly for every later choice.
The types ι and Ω are arbitrary and may live in independent universe levels.
ι is equipped with a Fintype instance but no explicit nonemptiness assumption.
Ω is equipped with an arbitrary measurable-space structure.
μ is an arbitrary measure on Ω equipped with an IsProbabilityMeasure instance.
X, m, M, and t are universally quantified implicit parameters inside the universal assertion.
All five displayed assumptions after the binders form an implication chain whose final consequent is the probability inequality.
Every finite sum is over all i ∈ ι via Finset.univ.
The integral is taken separately for each i with respect to μ and is the Bochner integral of the real-valued function X_i.
The event concerns the sum of centered variables X_i - ∫X_i dμ.
GE.ge makes the event condition exactly 'centered sum ≥ t', not the reversed inequality.
The numeral 2 occurs both as the exponent in squares and as the multiplicative prefactor outside exp.
The exponent is the negative real number -(c t²/S).
translation.proposition_plain_english: There exists a universal real constant c > 0 such that, for every finite index type ι, every measurable space Ω, every probability measure μ on Ω, every finite family X = (X_i) of real-valued measurable functions that is mutually independent under μ, every pair of real endpoint families m = (m_i) and M = (M_i), and every real threshold t, if X_i lies in the closed interval [m_i,M_i] μ-almost everywhere for every i, t > 0, and the sum S = ∑_{i∈ι} |M_i-m_i|² is positive, then μ({ω ∈ Ω | ∑_{i∈ι}(X_i(ω) - ∫_Ω X_i(y) dμ(y)) ≥ t}), regarded as a real number, is at most 2 exp(-c t²/S).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: If ι is empty, S is the empty sum 0, so the hypothesis S > 0 is false and the implication is vacuous.
If every interval has zero width, then S = 0 and the implication is vacuous.
If some m_i > M_i, the closed interval [m_i,M_i] is empty. For a probability measure the asserted almost-everywhere membership is then impossible, so that instance is vacuous.
The explicit hypothesis S > 0 excludes division by zero in every nonvacuous application, even though Lean's real division is total.
No ordering assumption m_i ≤ M_i is separately stated; it is only forced in nonvacuous cases by the almost-everywhere interval hypothesis.

No integrability hypothesis is written explicitly. Measurability, almost-everywhere boundedness, finiteness of the index family, and the probability-measure assumption supply the expected mathematical setting for the displayed integrals.
The conclusion is only an upper-tail estimate; it does not directly state an absolute-value or two-sided deviation event despite the prefactor 2.
The proposition asserts existence of some positive uniform constant and does not specify its numerical value.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the target itself and fixes all quantifiers, hypotheses, and the conclusion translated above.
